beats.say: In 1918 a secret pact between the Ukrainian People's Republic and Germany turned Kyiv into a hidden chessboard of ambition.
The Germans supplied 30,000 rifles, but demanded the right to station troops near the Dnieper, hoping to secure grain routes.
Ukrainian commander Symon Petliura saw the aid as a double-edged sword, fearing his army would become a puppet militia.
When the Central Powers collapsed in November, the German troops vanished overnight, leaving the Ukrainian forces exposed and under-armed.
beats.visual: map of Central Powers collapse November 1918

beats.say: Petliura scrambled to negotiate with the advancing Bolsheviks, promising to cede the strategic port of Odesa for a ceasefire.
The secret clause revealed Germany planned to install a pro-Berlin monarch from the Hohenzollern house.
Ukrainian historians later called it the 'forgotten coup', because the monarch never arrived, yet the clause fueled internal dissent.
By spring 1919 the Ukrainian army fractured, with former German-trained units defecting to the Red Army, sealing the republic's downfall.
The episode shows foreign arms betraying a newborn state, turning hope into a tragic pawn on the Eastern Front.
